references.text: Zechariah prophesies about a future mourning in Jerusalem over "him whom they have pierced." The women who wept over Jesus on the way to Golgotha reflect this prophetic lament – [ref:Sak 12:10-14|Zechariah 12:10-14] describes deep sorrow divided among families and women separately, which corresponds with the women beating their breasts and mourning over Jesus.

Jesus answers the weeping women and tells them to weep for themselves and their children, foretelling Jerusalem's coming judgment. [ref:Luk 23:28-31|Luke 23:28-31] is the direct continuation and context for the women's lament in verse 27.

At the raising of Jairus' daughter, it is described that the crowd "wept and beat their breasts" (ἐκόπτοντο) over her. The same Greek verb is used in [ref:Luk 8:52|Luke 8:52], showing a parallel mourning ritual action in Luke's gospel.

After Jesus' death, the crowd beat their breasts and returned, while the women who had followed him from Galilee stood watching. [ref:Luk 23:48-49|Luke 23:48-49] completes the sorrow that began on the way to the cross and shows that the lament over Jesus continued through the crucifixion.

Jesus himself wept over Jerusalem and prophesied the city's destruction. [ref:Luk 19:41-44|Luke 19:41-44] forms the background for Jesus' words to the weeping women – sorrow over Jerusalem's fate is a recurring theme in Luke.

Jeremiah calls for professional mourners to hold a lament over the people. [ref:Jer 9:17-20|Jeremiah 9:17-20] (Hebrew 9:16-19) describes women who lament and weep in connection with judgment and destruction – a background for the women's mourning over Jesus on the way to crucifixion.

The prophet Joel calls for sorrow and lamentation: "Between the porch and the altar let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep." [ref:Joel 2:17|Joel 2:17] shows the collective lament in Israel over coming judgment, which is reflected in the people's sorrow over Jesus.

Matthew also mentions the many women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him, standing and watching the crucifixion. [ref:Matt 27:55-56|Matthew 27:55-56] is a parallel to the women who followed Jesus in Luke's account.

Mark also tells of women who followed Jesus and were present at the crucifixion. [ref:Mark 15:40-41|Mark 15:40-41] is a synoptic parallel confirming the women's faithful following of Jesus all the way to the cross.
